We absolutely loved this lollipop loop trail! Wow. What a gift. I believe a lot of hikers go to this trail to hike directly to the lookout point. So this means at the loop junction you would go to the left - which also means you will hike a pretty intense straight-up incline. If you have the time to spare, do the whole loop - meaning at the loop junction you’ll veer slight right. The loop brings you through diverse forest, apple trees, flowering meadows, magical rivers, bridges and boardwalks. You will encounter two long inclines that no doubt get the heart pumping and your bum muscles working…however, they are totally manageable. Some of the views along the way are breathtaking, but for sure the sweet cherry on top  of the loop is, of course, at the very end when you are gently delivered to Murphy’s Lookout. Wow. Unbelievable. After you soak in the view, you will steeply decline (and feel very thankful you are on the decline end of the stick vs inclining) and arrive back at the loop junction where you will make your way back to the trail head beginning about 1km.

Something to note, there are three areas to park - the most popular being where AllTrails navigates you - off of highway 19, where you will need to park on the side of the fast moving highway. The other two are tucked in along the trail. I loved hiking from the highway point, but if you’re worried about your car parked on the side of the road, take the time to check out the other two parking spots (indicated by orange dots on the map). I think that’s all, a really, really lovely hike.

Love this trail especially the lookout point (Murphy's) which will undoubtedly offer even better views in the coming days. Nice trail, good length. Nice view up top, some pretty creeks. Pretty quiet, only saw a few other people. 2 good parking options. Easy to turn 8km into 10+km loop.
The trail is awesome and has a nice lookout near the end of the hike. A great mix of bridges, branches, mud and a paved road. The downside is that it's really buggy during this time.

Nice trail, very buggy with deer flies.  Would give it a higher rating if not for the portion of road walking.   Nice mix of grass and forest, the streams on the south were nice.  Next time we'll go in the opposite direction to get the monotonous portions out of the way first.
A lot of bug. Need to bring bug spray. There is a big uphill on left side, personal feel better to go left first.

Trail is absolutely beautiful and leads to one of the best lookouts I’ve seen in a provincial park this close to the city. The trail is rough in some places with a lot of encroaching vegetation so make sure to check yourself and your pets for ticks after hiking. The elevation gain was hard in the heat today but was very doable for people with pets or children on a cooler day. There were some bugs but not an unbearable amount. There are many different places near the trail entrances to park, check the Bruce trail conservancy for more about parking spots. There is one small lot that is unsigned but quite a far walk from the trails. As this is a non-operating park, there is no fee to enter or use the Bruce trails within the park. There are no facilities at all, but there is a picnic spot with outhouses ten minutes from the park along Highway 10, or at super burger or champ burger five minutes away at 89 and 10.
Lovely trail, green and lush. Very quiet for a sunny Sunday morning.

Trail is ok. Completed with my 4 y/o daughter starting from the car park (adds a cpl extra kms). We went left (clockwise) up the steep climb to the look out first which was fun and had a nice view at the top.  The trail to the road is mostly open with little tree cover and follows along some farms. You will walk up a road to get back to the trail and we found the second half more enjoyable with more shade and some creeks and a bit of mud. We went up to the look out on the way back for another look of the view which is only slightly off course. Overall an ok trail. we went to Pretty river last week and though that was a bit nicer.
Very nice trail, great scenery. Lightly trafficked but I did it during the week.
Very nice!  Great lookout!  Nice diversity of forests.
So many different tree types, the valley and various scenery. I'd rate it as moderate.

A sometimes challenging hike due to the changes in elevation, especially to get to the lookout, which was worthwhile. Excellent variety in this hike to keep it interesting: forest, creeks, open meadows, a farmer's property adjacent at one point, some muddy spots. 

At about halfway through you find yourself on a roadway for approximately 500 meters.

Minimal insects.

nice challenging trail. lovely vistas and stunning view from the top of the lookout. some of the elevations - up and down - were challenging due to the degree change but manageable. nice trail, would love to do it in the fall as the colours change

The weather was perfect when we started out on the trail. Mid-way there was a drizzle which just added to the beauty of the trail. Bruce Trail loop was exhilarating but worth our time and energy. The view from the top of the kame was breathtaking! Though the trail loop is 8kms we ended up walking extra 2 kms. The best part about the trail is the walk among those tall trees listening to nothing but the music of nature.

This was a nice trail. I recommend when you get to the field with the folk, don't go left, but go right. I went up the steep hill to the look out. The look out was breath taking, but you can always go back to it when you go right. And since I went left, I missed the bridge and started to go on the Bruce Trail that was muddy and turned into a brook. I stayed on the Primose trail and didnt do the whole 8km loop. Overall it was a nice trail after I found my way. Muddy at times and some bugs.

Lovely trails with some steep inclines. Was very muddy in some areas. No one social distanced that I encountered except myself. I had to walk off the trail to avoid them or wore my mask when I couldn’t. Very disappointed, won’t go back until people act responsibly & respectfully

Run this trail often. one of my favourites! watch out for the hill of despair after some pretty bridges! There's is also a porcupine that lives in a hollowed out tree roughly 1.5km down the trail in the forest after the farm field. watch your pup especially if they are off leash.

Beautiful trail, well marked and extremely clean! Great for kids and dog. We went in the beginning of March and it was pretty icy in some spots (be careful with children!!!). It can get a little steep in some areas that are then exasperated by the ice but go slow and it’s totally doable. We went with a dog and an 8 year old and while  it took us a bit longer, it was manageable. Lots of creeks to cross but all of them are very crossable! Part of the trail runs on a service road (700 m?) but it’s quick and we only saw 1 car. Be mindful of dogs off leash here, there are many regulars that do not leash their dogs.
